sents: Guan-guan go the ospreys, on the islet in the river.
The modest, retiring, virtuous, young lady: for our prince a good mate she.
Here long, there short, is the duckweed, to the left, to the right, borne about by the current.
The modest, retiring, virtuous, young lady: waking and sleeping, he sought her.
He sought her and found her not, and waking and sleeping he thought about her.
Long he thought; oh! long and anxiously; on his side, on his back, he turned, and back again.

overrides.description: A classical Chinese poem in English translation; each stanza is numbered as a paragraph

batches.assembled_prompt:
A classical Chinese poem in English translation; each stanza is numbered as a paragraph; each paragraph starts with its number:

[P1] Guan-guan go the ospreys, on the islet in the river. The modest, retiring, virtuous, young lady: for our prince a good mate she.

[P2] Here long, there short, is the duckweed, to the left, to the right, borne about by the current. The modest, retiring, virtuous, young lady: waking and sleeping, he sought her.

[P3] He sought her and found her not, and waking and sleeping he thought about her. Long he thought; oh! long and anxiously; on his side, on his back, he turned, and back again.

For each paragraph, look at its last sentence: does it open something the reader now waits for, and does the next paragraph take that up? Spelling and grammar do not count.
Offences, scored 0 to 9 as how likely a reader of this poem is to meet the problem at this sentence:
1 forgotten beat: wonders whether the writer forgot to follow up what the sentence before set up
2 unanchored reference: has to search for what a word (a name, "we", "this", a term) refers to
3 missing link: has to work out alone how this sentence connects to the one before
4 out of order: meets this sentence before something it depends on
5 repetition: feels told something they were already told
6 contradiction: notices this sentence conflicts with something earlier
7 purpose unclear: cannot see what this sentence does for the point being made
8 register shift: notices the voice change, for example from telling a story to lecturing
9 long dependency: has to hold words in mind because the words that belong together sit far apart
Write a TSV and nothing else. One row per sentence where any offence scores 2 or more, in reading order: paragraph.sentence (sentence position within the paragraph, e.g. 3.2), TAB, the nine scores comma-separated in the order above, TAB, why in at most 15 words (for offence 2 name the word). Last line: END.

3.why: Duckweed image given without a stated link to the lady or prince

4.why: Refrain repeats 1.2 verbatim; "he" taken to mean the prince, never confirmed

5.why: Restates "he sought her" and "waking and sleeping" from 2.2

6.why: Ends on unresolved longing; nothing follows; "long he thought" echoes 3.1
